cohort: Female rats from three strains (inbred Genetic Absence Epilepsy Rats From Strasbourg (GAERS), inbred Non-Epileptic Controls (NEC), and outbred nonepileptic Wistars) were fed standard chow or VPA mixed in chow for 2 weeks prior to conception and throughout pregnancy.
finding: Gestational sodium valproate (VPA) treatment resulted in significant developmental and morphological abnormalities, including reduced weight, length, and underdeveloped vertebral arches, in all three rat strains, suggesting that the genetic underpinnings of epilepsy do not substantially contribute to VPA-induced birth defects.
